Guidance & outlook: I am happy to say that we achieved our targets for FY26 and are well on our way to achieving our targets for FY27.
We are targeting 10% to 15% ARR growth on the domestic portfolio.

So if I'm understanding you correctly, if even in the first half of FY27 if we have a revenue of like INR70 crores, these other expenses would not be INR36 crores because, INR3.5 crores GST would deduct, which is like INR32.5 crores, and also it will reduce in the first half, further than that.
Growth & demand: Revenue from operations in the financial year '26 came at INR114 crores, which is a 44% growth in a single year.
PAT, Profit after tax, grew 19% to INR18 crores from INR15.5 crores last year.
Despite all of this, the company managed to deliver 44% growth over the last year with a CAGR of 30% on revenue and 25% on EBITDA.
Margins & costs: EBITDA margins for the current year is 23.1% versus 30% last year.

In September '25, the Government of India notified GST 2.0, and the rates of the hospitality hotels which are priced below INR7,500 per night were revised from 12% with input tax credit to 5% without input tax credit.
The H2 impact for us was approximately INR3.5 crores, directly impacting our EBITDA margins.
Capex & expansion: This year, we at Suba Hotels invested in further strengthening our foundation by investing in people, process, technology, including AI, to build a future -ready organization that can absorb and support the growth.

Also, we have around 20 hotels coming in the next year -- in this current year, which will and further two hotels which are renovated, which will be back at full capacity, to drive our margins and economies of scale.
But in your PPT I can see your franchise at 51% of the portfolio and it shows very high EBITDA margin with low capex, but you are saying you are focused on the revenue share preferably.
Balance sheet & cash: We are going forward without taking any disproportionate leverage and remaining capital light.
Second question is, so though we are having profits, but the cash flow is seriously negative.
So the cash flow in the current year what we are saying is INR57 crores, it includes the movement from fixed deposits.
Risks & challenges: All of this was delivered in a single year where the industry witnessed multiple challenges like geopolitical situations during the India -Pak war in the month of May, Air India crash, Indigo airline fiasco, GST 2.0, and lastly, the Middle East crisis, which impacted our UAE operations.
One of the reasons for the margin contraction is our UAE operations, which got softe r at a later part of the year due to the ongoing Gulf conflict.
With all those headwinds mostly removed and 22 hotels coming in the next year, we are absolutely optimistic for what lies ahead for us.

Of these 901 pipeline keys, we expect approximately 850, that's over 94%, around 95%, to become operational within just the next 12 months.
Looking ahead, we anticipate 10% to 15% ARR growth next year, complemented by 5% to 7% occupancy percent gain, driven by our strategic initiatives.
Growth & demand: The growth has been achieved while adding approximately 528 keys post -IPO, with over 85% of that expansion being asset -light.
With 18 hotels and 901 keys in the pipeline, we're looking at a 20% expansion without putting stress on this balance sheet.
EBITDA grew 54%, and PAT grew 58%, with margins expanding across the board.
Margins & costs: Our experience in these markets gives us strong visibility on demand patterns, pricing behavior, and operating economics.
Leases and revenue-shared structures form the core of our expansion, structured conservatively to protect downside while delivering strong EBITDA.

These markets typically exhibit lower land costs and operational efficiencies, limited branded supply, and stable domestically driven market that collectively support healthier margins and faster breakeven points for us.
Capex & expansion: Capacity additions, new brands, and rapid expansion have dominated the conversation.
Geographically, our expansion strategy is both diversified and disciplined.

In 2025, India's travel and tourism GDP grew 7.3%, broadly in line with the 7.5% overall GDP growth, reinforcing its position as the third-largest tourism economy in the Asia-Pacific region.
Revenue from operations grew 44.3% to ₹11,435.28 lakhs, EBITDA grew 15.2% to ₹2,681.79 lakhs and profit after tax grew 18.9% to ₹1,801.28 lakhs.
Margins & costs: Operating costs and margin EBITDA rose 15.2% to ₹2,681.79 lakhs.

Cost of materials consumed in fact improved as a proportion of revenue, to 8.3% from 9.4%, and employee benefits expense was broadly stable at 20.4% of total revenue against 20.2%, indicating that the margin movement is not a function of wage or input cost inflation.

Operating profit margin (EBITDA %) 23.14% 29.09% (20.5)% Higher operating costs and margin pressure due to GST changes disallowing Input Tax Credit, increased contribution from lease/ revenue-share properties bearing full operating costs, and ramp-up costs as newly added hotels remain in the stabilization phase.
Capex & expansion: Our expansion strategy remains agile and capital- conscious, spanning greenfield, brownfield and conversion projects.
Our current pipeline reflects this approach, with approximately 60% comprising conversion projects and 40% greenfield developments.

Growth was broad-based: manufacturing expanded in double digits, Private Final Consumption Expenditure accelerated to 7.7% from 5.8%, and Gross Fixed Capital Formation grew 8.2%, reflecting the continued public capital expenditure cycle.
Balance sheet & cash: Current ratio (times) 2.22 0.70 +215.15% Reflects the receipt of issue proceeds during the year, a consequent increase in current assets, and the repayment of short-term borrowings, which together moved the Company from a negative to a comfortable net working capital position.

Debt-equity ratio (times) 0.37 1.05 (64.6)% Net worth increased approximately 2.9 times to ₹13,816.31 lakhs on the issue of equity share capital and retention of profits, while total borrowings were broadly unchanged.

Cash flow from operating activities includes ₹3,766 lacs towards placement of fixed deposits with banks (grouped under other current assets) and ₹1,336 lacs towards capital advances (grouped under short term loans and advances).
Risks & challenges: Inventory remains immaterial at ₹45.99 lakhs, or 0.2% of total assets, so the ratio is volatile and not indicative of any change in operating efficiency.
RISK MANAGEMENT: Your Company has a well-defined risk management framework in place to identify, assess the key risks and mitigate them appropriately.

The Company has reviewed the major risks, including risks on account of business continuity, supply chain management, third- party risks, legal compliance and other risks which may affect or have affected its employees, customers and all other stakeholders from both the external and the internal environment perspective.
